questions.stem: A an outlier and a valid extreme case records 61 and 10 and requires a decision. An unusually large frog turns up in a field sample. What is the right first move?

options.misconception: Assumes drop all extremes without checking outlier and a valid extreme

questions.explanation: Extremes may be valid or errors. Investigation precedes dropping. Automatic actions risk bias.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: Why distance-based methods need a common scale
questions.stem: A case study of why distance-based methods need a common scale supplies the data 62 and 11. One feature with a far wider range than the others is controlling a distance calculation. What is happening?

options.misconception: Assumes distance is scale-invariant without checking why distance-based methods need a common scale

questions.explanation: Large-range features dominate Euclidean distance. Importance is separate. Distance is not scale-invariant, so scaling is needed.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: Why gradient methods need a common scale
questions.stem: A worked why gradient methods need a common scale example uses the figures 63 and 12. A model converges much faster after every feature is put on a common scale. What does that demonstrate?

options.misconception: Assumes gradients ignore scale without checking why gradient methods need a common scale

questions.explanation: Gradient descent converges faster when features share a scale. Scaling does not change predictions, only optimization speed. Distance and gradient both benefit.
